task_completion.description: The 'Fluorescent Cells' sample image is opened in ImageJ.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The ImageJ workspace shows an image window titled 'FluorescentCells.jpg' or similar, displaying red and green cell structures.

task_completion.description: The original RGB image is split into individual Red, Green, and Blue channels.
task_completion.visual_evidence: Three separate grayscale image windows appear, typically labeled (red), (green), and (blue).

task_completion.description: The original Red channel data is assigned the Magenta color/LUT.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A channel settings or LUT menu shows the Red channel data being displayed as Magenta (a mix of red and blue pixels).

task_completion.description: The channels are merged back into a composite image using Magenta, Green, and Blue.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A 'Merge Channels' dialog box or a new composite image window where the previously red areas now appear magenta, and green areas remain green.

task_completion.description: The composite image is flattened into a standard RGB format.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The image window header changes from 'Composite' to 'RGB' or a 'Flatten' command is visible in the menu history.

task_completion.description: The final image is saved to the specific path ~/ImageJ_Data/results/accessible_composite.tif.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A 'Save As' dialog box or a file explorer window shows the file 'accessible_composite.tif' being saved in the 'results' directory.

integrity.description: The agent used the ImageJ GUI rather than just executing CLI scripts to process the image.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show the mouse cursor interacting with ImageJ menus (Image > Color > Split Channels, etc.) and dialog boxes.

integrity.description: The agent did not simply rename the source file or move a pre-existing result file.
integrity.visual_evidence: The sequence of screenshots shows the intermediate steps of channel splitting and color re-assignment within the ImageJ interface.

integrity.description: The final image shows the correct visual transformation (Red -> Magenta).
integrity.visual_evidence: The final saved image in the screenshot displays a clear magenta and green color scheme, distinct from the original red and green.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The source image 'FluorescentCells.jpg' is a 512x512 image. The task requires a specific color mapping: the original Red channel must become Magenta, while Green and Blue remain unchanged. Magenta in ImageJ is a combination of the Red and Blue display channels. The final output must be a flattened RGB TIFF file located at ~/ImageJ_Data/results/accessible_composite.tif.
